title: Regional Affinity Controller: latency-aware pinning with capacity demotion
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a Regional Affinity Controller (RAC) that combines latency-based routing, geo-pinning soft anchors, and capacity-aware demotion to meet P95 latency SLOs while minimizing cross-region churn and customer impact.

Scope: Design and implement a routing layer module that: 1) computes a per-customer region affinity score using realtime latency SLOs and historical latency distributions; 2) applies 'soft pinning' to prefer the home region when within headroom; 3) demotes affinity proactively when region capacity approaches critical thresholds; 4) integrates circuit-breaker signals and shedding policies to prevent cascading failures; 5) exposes diagnostics and tunable knobs in the Console for rollout.

Key design points: 
- Affinity score = weighted combination of: recent P95 delta vs SLO, smoothed tail latency, backend capacity utilization, and routing cost budget. Weights are configurable per-customer tier.
- Soft pinning: a hysteresis window prevents frequent flips; small latency regressions tolerated up to a per-customer budget before routing switches to alternate region.
- Capacity demotion: when allocation headroom < demotion_threshold (configurable, default 15%), reduce affinity proportionally and start hedged requests to secondary region for a sampled percentage to validate compatibility.
- Circuit breakers: integrate with existing circuit-breaker manager; if region CB trips for a model/route, RAC automatically rebalances and increments shedding priority.
- Load shedding: when global capacity is constrained, RAC applies progressive shedding starting with non-critical customers and degraded models; console shows projected customer impact.

Telemetry and SLOs: 
- Emit per-region affinity_change events, hedged_request_count, demotion_signals, and shed_decisions.
- Dashboards: per-customer P95, routing path distribution, demotion rate, and regional utilization.
- Alerting: SLO burn rate > 2x for 5min for a region triggers automated evaluation and candidate failover.

Rollout plan: 
1) Canary in single non-production org: enable RAC in 'observe-only' and emit affinity suggestions (2 weeks).
2) Gradual rollout to low-traffic customers with hedged requests enabled (4 weeks).
3) Expand to all customers with soft-pinning defaults and demotion thresholds enabled (2-6 weeks), monitor SLO and cost.

Compatibility: Works with hosted and Dedicated. Private deployments require policy sync; document KMS and network assumptions.

Risks: 
- Frequent region flips causing KV cache churn and higher p90 for new sessions. Mitigation: longer hysteresis and sampled hedging before full failover.
- Incorrect capacity signals causing unnecessary demotion. Mitigation: ensemble signals (alloc headroom + recent retry rates + infra health).
- Cost increase from hedged traffic. Mitigation: sampling and dynamic budget per customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: RAC module deployed behind feature flag with observe-only mode emitting affinity suggestions
Console dashboard shows affinity metrics and per-route demotion events
Canary customers show no regression in P95 beyond 5% vs baseline during hedged pilot
Demotion triggers prevent region overload in a synthetic overload test and reduce error rate by >= 30% vs baseline
Design doc, runbook, and rollback plan published in Confluence; PRs merged and QA tests added
